verdict.rationale: Vue's docs describe a 'truly reactive, compiler-optimized rendering system that rarely requires manual optimization', and its testing guide refers to Reactivity APIs used in composables. Hands-on community reports praise the reactivity API for component state, effects and computed values; one user notes it only tracks changes under certain conditions, which is a caveat rather than a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of dependency tracking and granular re-run behavior (ref/reactive/computed/watch semantics) in the pack, and independent confirmation that only dependent code re-runs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can declare reactive state and have only the dependent UI code re-run when it changes

citations.quote: Truly reactive, compiler-optimized rendering system that rarely requires manual optimization.
If a composable only uses Reactivity APIs, then it can be tested by directly invoking it and asserting its returned state/methods
Vue's reactivity API for component state, effects and computed values is more ergonomic than React's.
